problem:
For which of the following functions is it valid to differentiate under the integral sign?

- ${F}_{1}(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+tx)}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x,\,t\in (-1,1)$
- ${F}_{2}(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x-t}\,\text{d}x,\,t\in (1,2)$
- ${F}_{3}(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{|x-t|}}\,\text{d}x,\,t\in (0,1)$

feedback.problem: If $f(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x+y,$ use the differential $\text{d}f$ to estimate the change $Δf$ in the value of $f(x,y)$ from $(4\pi ,8)$ to $(13,8.5).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x+1\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(4\pi ,8),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(4\pi ,8) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡4\pi \,\text{d}x+1\,\text{d}y \\  & =0\,\text{d}x+1\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(4\pi +Δx,8+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈0\,Δx+1\,Δy.
$$

Moving from $(4\pi ,8)$ to $(13,8.5),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =13-4\pi , \\ Δy & =8.5-8=0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈0\,Δx+1\,Δy \\  & ≈0\cdot (13-4\pi )+1\cdot (0.5) \\  & ≈0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $f(x,y)$ increases by approximately $0.5.$
